title: The Circulatory System
hook: Your heart pumps blood through roughly 60,000 miles of vessels, delivering oxygen and fuel to every cell and hauling waste away — about once a minute.
key_points: The heart pumps blood through a closed loop of arteries, veins, and capillaries.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.
Blood delivers oxygen and nutrients and removes carbon dioxide and waste.
Red blood cells carry oxygen using the iron-rich protein hemoglobin.
content_html: The circulatory system is your body's transport network, and the heart is its pump. With each beat, the heart pushes blood through a closed loop of vessels that, laid end to end, would stretch tens of thousands of miles. Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart under pressure; veins return the spent blood; and microscopic capillaries bridge the two, thin enough for oxygen and nutrients to slip across into the surrounding cells.
extra_html: Blood is the cargo. Its red cells, loaded with the iron-rich protein hemoglobin, pick up oxygen in the lungs and release it wherever it's needed; on the return trip they help carry away carbon dioxide. The same circuit distributes nutrients from digested food, hormones, immune cells, and heat. It all ties back to cellular respiration: the oxygen your blood delivers is exactly what your cells use to burn fuel, and the carbon dioxide it removes is that process's waste. The NIH SEER training module diagrams the heart's chambers and the path blood takes through the body.

related.title: Cellular Respiration
related.hook: Every cell in your body slowly 'burns' sugar with oxygen to release energy — the same chemistry as photosynthesis, run in reverse.

related.title: Homeostasis: Staying Balanced
related.hook: Your body works hard to keep its inside world steady — temperature, water, blood sugar — no matter what's happening outside. That balancing act is homeostasis.

flashcards.prompt: What is the difference between arteries and veins?
flashcards.back_html: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back to the heart. Tiny capillaries connect the two and exchange materials with cells.

flashcards.prompt: What is the main job of the circulatory system?

choices.text: Transport oxygen, nutrients, and waste throughout the body
Send electrical signals to the muscles

flashcards.explanation_html: The circulatory system is the body's delivery and removal network, moving oxygen and fuel in and carrying waste out.

flashcards.prompt: What carries oxygen in the blood?
flashcards.explanation_html: Red blood cells are packed with hemoglobin, an iron-rich protein that binds oxygen and ferries it to tissues.
